To use the standard algorithm, the divisor must be a whole number.

Content:
So, to divide decimals by other decimals such as [MATH: 0.832 \div 0.13,] we must find an equivalent division problem by multiplying both the dividend and divisor by an appropriate power of ten.

Content:
First, we write the division problem [MATH: 0.832 \div 0.13] as a fraction:
[MATH: \dfrac{0.832}{0.13}]

Content:
Multiplying the numerator and denominator by [MATH: 100,] we get a whole number in the denominator:

Content:
[MATH: \dfrac{0.832 \times 100}{0.13 \times 100} = \dfrac{83.2}{13}]

Content:
So the problem is equivalent to [MATH: 83.2 \div 13.]

Content:
Next, we write down the problem using long division notation, where we keep the decimal point in the dividend:

Content:
| | [MATH: 13] | [MATH: \!\require{enclose}\enclose{longdiv}{8 {\:\phantom{|}} 3 {\,\bbox[2px, lightgray]{\color{blue}.}\,} 2}] | |

Content:
We also bring the decimal point up into the quotient, placing it directly above the dot in the dividend:

Content:
| | [MATH: \:\:\: \phantom{0} {\:\phantom{|}} \phantom{0} {\:\phantom{|}} \bbox[2px, lightgray]{\color{blue}.}] | / | [MATH: 13] | [MATH: \!\require{enclose}\enclose{longdiv}{8 {\:\phantom{|}} 3 {\,\bbox[2px, lightgray]{\color{blue}.}\,} 2}] | |

Content:
Now, сarrying out the long division process as usual, we get:

Content:
| | | | [MATH: 6] | [MATH: \!\!\! . 4] | / | [MATH: 13] | [MATH: \!\!\require{enclose}\enclose{longdiv}{8 {\:\phantom{|}} 3 {\, . \,} 2}] | / | [MATH: -\!\!\!\!] | [MATH: 7] | [MATH: 8] | | / | | | [MATH: 5] | [MATH: 2] | / | | [MATH: -\!\!\!\!] | [MATH: 5] | [MATH: 2] | / | | | [MATH: \phantom{0}] | [MATH: 0] | |

Content:
Therefore,
[MATH: 0.832 \div 0.13 = 6.4\,.]

To use the standard algorithm, the divisor must be a whole number.

So, to divide decimals by other decimals such as [MATH: 0.832 \div 0.13,] we must find an equivalent division problem by multiplying both the dividend and divisor by an appropriate power of ten.

Multiplying the numerator and denominator by [MATH: 100,] we get a whole number in the denominator:

Content:
| | [MATH: \:\:\: \phantom{0} {\:\phantom{|}} \phantom{0} {\:\phantom{|}} \bbox[2px, lightgray]{\color{blue}.}] | / | [MATH: 13] | [MATH: \!\require{enclose}\enclose{longdiv}{8 {\:\phantom{|}} 3 {\,\bbox[2px, lightgray]{\color{blue}.}\,} 2}] | |

Content:
Now, сarrying out the long division process as usual, we get:

Content:
| | | | [MATH: 6] | [MATH: \!\!\! . 4] | / | [MATH: 13] | [MATH: \!\!\require{enclose}\enclose{longdiv}{8 {\:\phantom{|}} 3 {\, . \,} 2}] | / | [MATH: -\!\!\!\!] | [MATH: 7] | [MATH: 8] | | / | | | [MATH: 5] | [MATH: 2] | / | | [MATH: -\!\!\!\!] | [MATH: 5] | [MATH: 2] | / | | | [MATH: \phantom{0}] | [MATH: 0] | |

Therefore,
